annotations.title: General Assembly Adopts Resolution Calling upon States Not to Recognize Changes in Status of Crimea Region | Meetings Coverage and Press Releases

content.text:
**Legally under international law: no — Crimea is internationally recognized as part of Ukraine, not Russia.**

Russia has **occupied and claimed to annex Crimea since 2014**, and it controls the peninsula in practice. But the **UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity** and called on states not to recognize changes to Crimea’s status after the 2014 referendum, which it described as invalid. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai))

So the short version is:

- **De jure / legally:** Crimea belongs to **Ukraine**.
- **De facto / on the ground:** Crimea is **controlled by Russia**.
- **Russia’s position:** Crimea is part of Russia.
- **Most of the international community’s position, including the U.S. and EU:** Russia’s annexation is illegal and Crimea remains Ukrainian territory. ([travel.state.gov](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/international-travel/International-Travel-Country-Information-Pages/Ukraine.html?utm_source=openai))
